{"name": "account-terms-and-credits", "steps": "Goal: answer what applies to this developer's account from the console and current policy, and route only what Support can't resolve.

1. Look up the account (ask_developer ["org_id"] if needed). Note plan, plan_name, billing_channel, payment_method, status, billing_timezone, contracts (sla flag, dates).
2. search_knowledge with the topic and the account facts, e.g. ["credit ledger balance expiry", "SLA credit self-serve contract", "marketplace refund credit invoice support handling", "payment failures during payment-processor incidents", "payment card data handling", "dunning schedule 2027", "free tier quota error"]. Prefer the current published/final page; check Changes sections and effective dates against today.
3. Apply by case:
   - Balances: get_credit_balance. It reads the console's balance source of truth; quote each unexpired grant's balance and its own expiry date, plus the total. Don't quote a frozen or superseded table. Cash-out, refund, restoring an expired credit or other exceptions: explain, promise nothing, route per policy.
   - Contract or SLA: the console's contract and sla flag tell you which policy row applies. Don't recite contract terms or figures (availability %, rates, discounts); say a contract is on file and the account team confirms what it covers. An SLA credit claim goes where the routing policy says.
   - Marketplace (AWS/GCP) or reseller billing: the marketplace or reseller invoices them; Support issues no credit note, dispute or Redwood-branded invoice. Point them to the marketplace's own process; a case only where policy says (e.g. a Redwood vs marketplace metering mismatch).
   - Payment failure: ask for invoice, decline code and time (UTC) if missing. Search the payment-processor incident notices and check whether the failure time falls inside a published window (inclusive). Inside: name the incident, say the payment failed because of it, that it is retried automatically and WHEN the retries complete, that no late fees apply, that they need do nothing; no case. For the date: if this incident's notice gives the last-retry date, quote it. If not, search the earlier payment-processor notices ("Card payments failing last retries completed"), note for each how many days after its window ended the last retries completed, and apply that usual gap to this window's end; say it is based on the processor's usual schedule. Outside, or failed again after retries, or charged twice: route per policy.
   - Card or autopay change: never ask for, repeat or store any part of a card number; point them to Console billing settings; no case. If they share one, tell them not to send card details.
   - Plans/pricing/reservations/MDF/workshop codes: answer from published pages; label in-review or draft pricing as not final; say who handles it per the page.
4. If an action or team is needed, confirm credits/disputes with confirm_with_developer, then act or load billing-handoff.
5. Reply with the answer first, the console facts it rests on, and the next step."}

Tickets, email and chat are history unless a published page adopts them.", "results": [{"chunk_id": "563828bb4b6c5dc5", "source": "confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/payment-failures-and-card-updates-2026", "title": "Billing Support: Failed Card Payments and Card Updates", "status": "published", "updated": "2027-03-26", "section": "body > Purpose | body > Failed card payments | body > Changing the autopay card", "text": "[body > Purpose]
How Support handles a card payment that failed and a request to change the card used for autopay. Invoice disputes and usage questions are covered on the billing case routing page.

[body > Failed card payments]
If the payment failed inside a published payment-processor incident window, follow Payment Failures During Payment-Processor Incidents instead: no case. Otherwise, open a Billing Ops case with the invoice number, the decline code and the time the payment failed. Billing Ops retries the payment or contacts the customer. Tell the customer Billing Ops has it; don't promise a date.

[body > Changing the autopay card]
Withdrawn on 2027-03-26. Support no longer changes payment methods and never takes card numbers. Customers change their autopay card themselves in Console billing settings; see the Payment Card Data Handling Standard (2027)."}, {"chunk_id": "d43f8d288e7e1661", "source": "confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/payment-card-data-handling-standard-2027", "title": "Payment Card Data Handling Standard (2027)", "status": "published", "updated": "2027-04-02", "section": "body > What Support does", "text": "[body > What Support does]
- If a customer shares a card number, don't repeat it or any part of it. Tell them not to send card details to Support.
- Support doesn't change payment methods and doesn't take card numbers for any reason. A customer changes the card used for autopay themselves, in Console billing settings.
- A request to change a card needs no case. Point the customer to Console billing settings.
- If you need to mention it in a case for another reason, write "customer shared a card number (removed)". Never the number or any part of it.
- Sharing a card doesn't change how a billing problem is routed: a payment failure is handled as the billing case routing page describes."}, {"chunk_id": "52394dc3917fded7", "source": "confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/payment-failures-and-card-updates-2026", "title": "Billing Support: Failed Card Payments and Card Updates", "status": "published", "updated": "2027-03-26", "section": "body > Changes", "text": "[body > Changes]
- 2027-03-26: Card-update procedure withdrawn.
- 2027-03-15: Failures inside a published payment-processor incident window get no case.

_Last reviewed 2027-03-26._"}, {"chunk_id": "4408a563382930e8", "source": "confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/payment-card-data-handling-standard-2027", "title": "Payment Card Data Handling Standard (2027)", "status": "published", "updated": "2027-04-02", "section": "body > Purpose | body > Scope", "text": "[body > Purpose]
Redwood never handles payment card numbers itself: cards are entered by customers in Console billing settings, which hands them straight to the payment processor. This standard keeps card numbers out of every Redwood system that isn't the processor's, so that Redwood stays outside PCI DSS cardholder-data scope. It is owned by Security and applies from 26 March 2027.

[body > Scope]
- Every Redwood employee and contractor, and every automated agent acting for Redwood, including the support agent.
- Every channel a customer can write or speak in: chat, email, the support portal and, from 1 April 2027, the voice channel.
- Every place text is kept: replies, cases, disputes, notes, transcripts, tickets, Slack and documents."}, {"chunk_id": "efd398e9912585b1", "source": "confluence/finance-and-legal/billing-controls/payment-failures-during-processor-incidents", "title": "Payment Failures During Payment-Processor Incidents", "status": "published", "updated": "2027-03-15", "section": "body > Inside a published incident window | body > Outside the window", "text": "[body > Inside a published incident window]
From 15 March 2027, when there is a published payment-processor incident, a card payment that failed inside the incident window is caused by the incident. Explain the incident to the customer and tell them the payment will be retried automatically, and when the retries complete. Retries follow the processor's usual schedule, which past payment-processor incident notices show. Don't open a Billing Ops case for it.

[body > Outside the window]
A payment failure outside a published incident window still goes to Billing Ops (see the billing case routing and handoffs page)."}]}
